card: **кото́рый** (*who, which, that*) takes its **gender and number** from the noun it refers to, but its **case** from its own role in the relative clause: **Э́то де́вушка, кото́рая живёт ря́дом** (subject: nominative) / **кото́рую я люблю́** (object: accusative) / **с кото́рой я рабо́таю** (after **с**: instrumental).

sections.body: **кото́рый** is an adjective-pronoun with two loyalties. It points back to a noun in the main clause, so it copies that noun's gender and number. But it also has a job inside its own clause (subject, object, after a preposition), and that job sets the case. Ask two questions: *which noun?* → gender/number; *what does it do in its clause?* → case.

head: Role in the clause
Example
rows: **Э́то друг, о кото́ром я тебе́ расска́зывал.**
**Э́то друг, брат кото́рого живёт в Ки́еве.**

sections.title: Punctuation and word order
sections.body:
- The relative clause is always set off by commas, on both sides if the sentence continues: **Кни́га, кото́рую ты дал, о́чень интере́сная.**
- A preposition goes in front of **кото́рый**, never at the end of the clause: **го́род, в кото́ром я живу́** (never *which I live in*).
- **что** can replace **кото́рый** in casual speech only in the nominative/accusative: **кни́га, что ты дал** (colloquial).
- After **тот**, **всё**, **ка́ждый** and similar words, use **кто** / **что** instead: **тот, кто зна́ет**; **всё, что я зна́ю**.

English *that* never changes and you can even drop it (*the book I read*). Russian **кото́рый** can never be dropped, and must be declined. The English habit of ending a clause with a preposition (*the city I live in*) has no Russian equivalent: the preposition jumps to the front.

mistakes.wrong: Э́то фильм, кото́рый я говори́л о.
mistakes.right: Э́то фильм, о кото́ром я говори́л.
mistakes.why: The preposition comes first and sets the case.
In its clause it's the object: accusative.

examples.ru: Я зна́ю челове́ка, кото́рый тебе́ помо́жет.
examples.en: I know someone who can help you.

examples.ru: Где кни́га, кото́рую я тебе́ дал?
examples.en: Where's the book I gave you?

examples.ru: Го́род, в кото́ром я живу́, о́чень краси́вый.
examples.en: The city I live in is very beautiful.

examples.ru: Э́то челове́к, с кото́рым я рабо́таю.
examples.en: This is the person I work with.

examples.ru: Де́ти, кото́рые игра́ют на у́лице, — мои́.
examples.en: The children playing outside are mine.
